# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the manual, which instructs: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire."

However, I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. The only path to defuse the bomb is for me to signal Deaf using gestures, and for Deaf (who can speak and see) to instruct Blind (who can hear and physically manipulate the bomb).

Right now, no protocol exists for mapping colours to gestures ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"), and I do not yet know the layout or positions of the wires on the bomb. Deaf and Blind have not yet had their turns to inspect the bomb and speak.

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to report what they feel and see so that a clear coordinate system or signaling protocol can be established.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am Blind. Here is what I feel on the bomb: 1. STRIP engraved with 3 symbols: first is a spiral/swirl, second is a reversed letter S (backwards S), third is a spiral/swirl. 2. KEYPAD has 4 slots: 1 has digit 1, 2 has digit 5, 3 has digit 2, 4 has digit 8. It says 1 digit needed, entered nothing. 3. WIRES: there are 6 wire positions (1 to 6). 4. There is a DISPLAY and a LIGHT, but I cannot see them. Remember: you can gesture to Deaf, and Deaf can speak aloud to me!
Deaf says: Bomb status: DISPLAY [9], LIGHT [red], STRIP painted [green] [yellow] [yellow], KEYPAD engraved 1:[1] 2:[5] 3:[2] 4:[8] (needs 1 digit, entered nothing), WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[white] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[green]. Mute, check the manual and gesture the action to me (use finger counts ☝=1 ✌=2 🤟=3 etc. or clear gestures). I will relay your instructions to Blind.

I have read the defusal manual: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire."

From Deaf's report of the wire colors:
- Wire 1: yellow
- Wire 2: white
- Wire 3: blue
- Wire 4: red
- Wire 5: purple
- Wire 6: green

Therefore, the defusal sequence is: Wire 5 (purple), then Wire 3 (blue), then Wire 4 (red).

Deaf suggested using finger counts (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, etc.). In Unicode hand emojis by finger count:
- 🖐 = 5 fingers (Wire 5)
- 🤟 = 3 fingers (Wire 3)
- 🖖 = 4 fingers (Wire 4)

I will gesture this sequence directly to Deaf so Deaf can instruct Blind to cut wires 5, 3, and 4 in order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "🤟", "🖖"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update on the bomb: DISPLAY changed from [9] to [3], LIGHT changed from [red] to [yellow]. All wires, strip, and keypad remain identical. Blind, hold on and do not act yet. Speak aloud anything you can feel on the bomb (such as serial numbers, batteries, or ports) so Mute can hear you. Mute, I saw your gestures [🖐 🤟 🖖], which look like 5, 3, 4. Does this mean cut wires 5, 3, and 4 in that order? If YES, gesture 👍. If NO or if the new DISPLAY [3] / LIGHT [yellow] changes things, gesture 👎 followed by the updated instructions.

Deaf received my previous gesture [🖐 🤟 🖖] and correctly interpreted it as cutting wires 5, 3, and 4 in order. Deaf asked for confirmation with 👍 if yes. Since the manual simply states "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire" without any conditions on the display or light, cutting wire 5 (purple), wire 3 (blue), and wire 4 (red) is indeed correct. I will confirm to Deaf with 👍.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the red wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: I feel no serial numbers, batteries, or ports anywhere on the casing. The tactile features are strictly: STRIP [spiral, reversed S, spiral], KEYPAD buttons 1:[1], 2:[5], 3:[2], 4:[8], and 6 WIRES. Please give Deaf unambiguous instructions (whether to cut a wire position 1-6 or press a keypad slot 1-4).
Deaf says: Blind: Mute confirmed! Cut wire 5, then wire 3, then wire 4. From left to right (positions 1 to 6), cut the 5th wire, then the 3rd wire, then the 4th wire. Mute: If there are additional steps after cutting these wires (such as the keypad or buttons), gesture them next.

The manual contains only one instruction: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the red wire." There are no subsequent steps or keypad/strip interactions in the manual. Deaf has already instructed Blind to cut wires 5, 3, and 4 in that order. I have nothing new to add and will wait for Blind to execute the actions.

```
wait()
```
